one_line: Write the closing three sections of the M3 execution plan — the risk register, the open-question table a maintainer can answer in one sitting, and the definition of done — with every file:line re-checked against the actual tree, plus a corrections table for the 13 anchors the plan got wrong (two of which, as written, would send an engineer to the wrong line or chase a phantom violation).
user_visible_effect: none — internal. No code, no runtime behaviour changes. The reader is the maintainer on Monday morning: P0 and P1 must be answerable from this document alone, and no anchor in it may point at a line that no longer says what the plan claims it says.

steps.instruction: Re-read plan lines 7615-7691 (this item's own text: §9 twelve risks, §10 twelve open questions, §11 twelve completion clauses plus the M3-C2 slip sentence) and lines 7473-7539 (§7 the eleven gates G1-G11 that §11's clauses restate). Do not paraphrase from memory — the whole point of this item is that the plan's text has drifted from the tree.

Re-run, from the repo root, the two gates the plan says are already RED before the work, and paste their real output into 90-back3.md. G4: `{ grep -rn "event\.wheel \* [0-9]" packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'; grep -rn "delta \* [0-9]" packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'; } | grep -v "^packages/tui/src/mouse-wheel\.ts:" | wc -l` must print 9. G5: the bash block in §7.1 must print 10 lines with `left=7` and `kept=3`. Both were reproduced at HEAD 808b365 while writing this spec; a maintainer should be able to reproduce them in under a minute. If either prints a different number, the tree moved since this spec was written and 90-back3.md must say so.

Run the plan's own hygiene gate and record that it is WRONG: `git grep -rn 'mock.module' packages/coding-agent/test packages/tui/test` returns 2 hits, both comments that warn against the practice (`packages/coding-agent/test/tools/lsp-regressions.test.ts:111` and `packages/tui/test/loop-watchdog-wiring.test.ts:13`). Replace G10 everywhere it appears (§7.1 and §11 clause 10) with a form that excludes prose: `git grep -rn 'mock\.module(' -- packages/coding-agent/test packages/tui/test` must return 0. Carrying the plan's literal form would send a compliant implementer hunting a violation that does not exist.

Write §9 Rủi ro as a consolidated table, not the plan's 12-item list. Six rows, one per failure mode that actually ends the milestone: (a) building something that already exists — verified true, the quota reader, the working-message override and the loop watchdog are all in the tree, so the checklist must name what was confirmed rather than what is missing; (b) a countdown cache-pill — the hit-rate arithmetic at segments.ts:718-735 is `cacheRead / (cacheRead + cacheWrite + input) * 100` and nothing else, so any TTL is a number that means nothing; (c) ordering — A2 must land in the same commit as D1, handler second-half included, because advertising an MCP capability with no handler makes a probing server worse off, not better; (d) the tool-renderer hole survives on an export-map wildcard (`packages/tui/package.json:93-96`) plus a loader remap closure (`packages/tui/src/tools/index.ts:73`), and a barrel refactor or an Object.freeze breaks it silently at plugin load — no Object.freeze exists today, verified; (e) chrome-scroll leaking into the main transcript, whose no-scroll-state invariant is documented at docs/tui-core-renderer.md:174 and never to be relaxed; (f) the M2 boundary — see step 5. Name the per-item risk only where it is not already covered by one of the six.

Correct risk #9 before writing it down. The plan says six of fifteen execution items (A4, B1, B2, B3, C2, D2) cannot start until M2 finishes. A4 is not one of them: the plan's own A4 item and its §4 row 20 both say the DISPLAY half (`plugin-settings.ts:30`, `:166`) is unblocked and belongs to wave 1, because `plugin-settings.ts` appears nowhere in the M2 plan. Only A4's PERSIST half (`packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/manager.ts:942-949`) is blocked, and it is blocked on M2 WI-8a specifically, not on 'M2 finishing'. The correct blocked set is therefore five items — B1, B2, B3, C2, D2 — which is what §6's own effort split already says ('7 ngày ở 5 hạng mục bị M2 chặn'). Write the five, and write A4 as a two-halves row.

Write §10 Câu hỏi mở as one answerable table. Sort so the questions that block STARTING an item come first. Keep all twelve of the plan's entries; mark the four the plan already closes (B1 stays a hole with a pinning test, A7 anchors on the composer, O5's cross-package seam is settled, the M3-C1 status-line question moved to M2-OQ3) as closed in place rather than deleting them, because a reader who remembers the question needs to see where it went. Then add the two new ones this spec found. (a) Does P1's `usage` answer include the `custom` preset? The `custom` preset at `presets.ts:96-103` spreads `CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS`, which lives at `packages/tui/src/status-line/schema.ts:36-42` — so 'all seven presets' is edited in schema.ts, not presets.ts, and a maintainer answering 'full + nerd' has silently left `custom` behind unless the question says which. (b) Who decides what A4's persist half types to disk? The plan states the repo has no secret store to fall back to (`grep -c secret manager.ts` → 0, verified) and that the decision is A4's own to bring — so it is a named hole, not an omitted one.

Write §11 clause 1 so the P1 answer is checkable by name, not by paraphrase. The clause must name every preset the maintainer chose and must forbid `status` in any of them — `status` already renders through a separate keyed path at `packages/tui/src/status-line/component.ts:3065-3068` under a flag defaulting true at `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/settings.ts:262-265`, so adding it to a preset renders every hook status TWICE. Carry the two negative contracts verbatim in shape: at 80 columns with a full usage context the quota segment still renders, and with `ctx.usage` undefined the row renders byte-identical to before. Every preset outside the P1 set must also render byte-identical.

Write §11 clause 6 without inventing a mechanism. The plan is explicit that the negative contract depends on which of M2's three directions M2-OQ3 picks: under a `core:`/`ext:` prefix a bare id is rejected; under a map fallback it is an UNREGISTERED id that is rejected, at render time; under a generic `mode` reading there is no per-id registration to reject. §11 must say 'per the mechanism M2 fixed' and enumerate the three branches, not pick one. Add the positive half: the hit-rate segment reports the SAME number as the existing `cache_hit` segment and carries no countdown and no TTL label.

Write 90-back3.md from the plan_corrections list in this spec, verbatim on the evidence column — every one was reproduced at HEAD 808b365 with a real command. Do not soften them and do not drop the two that change what a gate does (the mock.module gate, and the A4 blocking contradiction). Add a one-line provenance note that these were measured on 808b365 on branch milestone-1, so a reader in three weeks knows when the table expires.

Write check-anchors.mjs (sketch in code_shape) so that every `file:line` in the three back-matter files is resolvable, and re-run it. It must exit 0 on what you wrote. Then deliberately break one anchor in a scratch copy and confirm it exits 1 — an anchor checker nobody has seen go red is not a gate.

Write assemble-m3.py and run it only once s1-s6 fragments exist. Until then, verify the script itself by pointing PARTS at the three back-matter files alone and confirming the guards fire correctly on a deliberately truncated input — the 800-byte and even-fence checks are the ones that catch a half-written agent turn.

test_contract:
No `.test.ts` is added or modified by this item, and none should be — this is a documentation work item and a new test that asserts the plan document says the right thing would be exactly the banned shape.

The observable contract is between the document and its reader, and it has two halves.

First, CITATION: every `file:line` in the three back-matter files resolves — the file exists and the cited range does not run past EOF. The consumer who regresses is the Monday implementer: a wrong anchor sends them to edit a line that has nothing to do with the feature, and the plan supplied 13 of them (see plan_corrections). Two are actively harmful rather than merely stale: the `mock.module` gate as written is RED on a fully compliant tree, and risk #9 would convince a maintainer that A4 is blocked when its own item text says the display half ships in wave 1.

Second, HONESTY: no gate in the closing sections may be stated as if it had been observed. G4 and G5 were run and are RED today; G1, G2, G3, G6-G9 and G11 were not run at all and the document must say so. If a reader trusts a gate that was never executed, the milestone reports green on work that never happened — the failure mode the M1 back matter's "Những điều chưa được kiểm chứng" section exists to prevent.

One asymmetry the engineer must preserve in the text: a counting gate is only a gate if it returns a NON-ZERO number today. G4 (9) and G5 (left=7) qualify. A gate phrased as 'the count is unchanged' is self-fulfilling and must be written the other way round — the plan itself makes this argument at length and then contradicts it in G10.

gate:
M3 is DONE when all four hold, and each can fail:

(1) `bun .lavish-wip/m3-md/check-anchors.mjs` exits 0 AND has been seen to exit 1. Checked anchors must number in the dozens, not zero — a back matter with no `file:line` in it has evaded the check rather than passed it.

(2) `python3 .lavish-wip/assemble-m3.py` refuses to run when fed a truncated part. The 800-byte and even-fence guards are the whole reason the script exists.

(3) `git grep -rn 'mock\.module(' -- packages/coding-agent/test packages/tui/test` returns 0, and the plan's uncorrected form (`mock.module`, no paren) is NOT what appears in 90-back1.md or 90-back2.md. This can fail: grep the back matter for the uncorrected token and it is found if someone copied §7 forward.

(4) Every claim in 90-back3.md's corrections table is reproducible on demand. Spot-check any three: run the command in the evidence column, get the same answer. A corrections table nobody spot-checked is worse than no corrections table, because it converts 'unverified' into 'asserted'.

Plus the two content gates, stated negatively: §10's table must contain a row for P0 and a row for P1 with a named owner and a deadline before A1 starts, and §11 must contain a clause naming the M3-C2 slip and a clause that A9 may NOT slip.
gate_can_fail: Yes, on every leg, and leg (1) fails in the most useful way. check-anchors.mjs is a plain script over files this item wrote: rename a cited file, move a cited line past EOF, or copy a stale anchor forward from the plan and it exits 1 with the offending citation named. The failure is guaranteed rather than hypothetical because this spec found 13 citations in the plan that are already wrong — so the corpus of anchors an implementer would copy forward is known-bad, and an uncorrected copy is detectable. Legs (2) and (3) are mechanical and were each run against a deliberately wrong input while writing this spec. Leg (4) is the only soft one: it is a discipline, not a script, and it can be satisfied by asserting something false. That is why the spec carries the evidence column verbatim with the exact command for each entry — a claim a reader can re-run in ten seconds is not the same as a claim someone merely typed.
depends_on: s1 — wave 1 items (A1 usage presets, A8 tmux key hints, A6 read-group membership, A5 stall indicator). §11 clauses 1, 2, 3, 7 and 9 are statements about s1's gates and cannot be written without them.

s5 — wave 5 items (A2 elicitation capability, C2 shell-call status strip, D2 hit-rate segment, D1 elicitation handler). §11 clauses 4 and 6 are about s5, and both of those clauses are void until M2-OQ3 has an answer — which is a dependency on M2, not on s5.
s6 — wave 6 (A9 daltonized theme). §11 clause 9 and the M3-C2 slip sentence both hinge on A9's S-versus-M decision, which §10 question 7 carries and nobody has answered.

P0 — the maintainer's written confirmation of the §8.2 spec table for A3, A7, A8, D2. Must be closed before wave 1 starts. tail2 cannot close it; it can only make it a table row with an owner and a deadline.

P1 — the maintainer's written answer to whether `usage` joins all seven status-line presets or a subset, naming each preset. Must be closed before A1 starts, and its answer is the target of §11 clause 1.

M2-OQ3 — the status-line extension-registration mechanism. §11 clause 6 is written as three branches precisely because this is unanswered; tail2 does not need the answer to write the clause, but s5 cannot implement C2 and D2 without it.
blocks: MILESTONE_3_EXECUTION_PLAN.md — the assembled execution plan. assemble-m3.py cannot run to completion until 90-back1/2/3.md exist.
M2 scheduling — §9 risk row (f) and §10 question 1 exist to answer 'what is M2's scope and exit criterion', which is the question that decides whether 7 engineer-days stay blocked.
effort: ~2 engineer-days. Roughly 0.5 day to re-verify and write the corrections table — most of that is already done here, and the evidence column is written out, so it is transcription plus a re-run. 0.5 day to write §9 and §10 as tables. 0.5 day to write §11 and the unverified section. 0.5 day to build and shake out check-anchors.mjs and assemble-m3.py. Not on the critical path for any code item: it can be written in parallel with s1-s6 and only needs to land before the plan is handed over.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is to write the closing sections as a faithful summary of the plan. That is the failure this whole item exists to prevent, and it is attractive precisely because it is easy: the plan's §9-§11 are already well-written, they read as authoritative, and copying them forward looks like diligence. The result would be a document in which thirteen citations are wrong, one gate is red on a compliant tree, and one risk entry contradicts the item text two hundred lines above it — all of it inherited, none of it visible unless a reader happens to open the cited file. The countermeasure is structural, not a reminder: every citation in the back matter is written so check-anchors.mjs resolves it, so a stale one cannot survive unnoticed, and the two gates whose failure modes are semantic rather than positional — the mock.module gate and the A4 blocking contradiction — are called out by name in 90-back3.md rather than left to be re-derived. A second, quieter way to get this wrong is to write §11 as a restatement of §7's gates. §7 states what a gate should be; §11 must state what must be true, and the two differ exactly where a gate is a bad instrument.
open_questions: P0 (blocking, owner: maintainer, in writing, due before wave 1 starts) — for A3, A7, A8 and D2: is the spec source `black-box` or `omp-native`, and where is the evidence? The §8.2 table proposes A7=omp-native, D2=omp-native, A8=black-box+omp-native, A3=omp-native-shape-plus-remeasured-constants. tail2 restates the table and puts it in a row with an owner; it cannot answer it.

P1 (blocking, owner: maintainer, in writing, due before A1 starts) — does `usage` join all seven status-line presets or a subset, naming each preset? tail2 additionally asks: does the answer include the `custom` preset? The `custom` entry at `packages/tui/src/status-line/presets.ts:96-103` spreads `CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS` from `packages/tui/src/status-line/schema.ts:36-42`, so including it means editing schema.ts, and excluding it must be said out loud — otherwise 'full and nerd' reads as a complete answer and quietly leaves `custom` on the old default list.

A9 S or M (owner: whoever schedules, due before A9 is planned) — extend the existing token list, or generate two hand-tuned themes through the OKLCH primitives already present at `packages/tui/src/theme/session-color.ts:2`? Default is M, ~5 days; S is ~1 day. The reason this must be decided rather than defaulted is the four-day spread, not that S is cheap. 99 palettes to touch either way (verified: `ls packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/*.json | wc -l` → 99).

A4 persist half (owner: the A4 implementer plus a reviewer, due before that half starts) — the repo has no secret store to fall back to. `grep -c secret packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/manager.ts` → 0 (verified), and the only keychain reference in the package is a browser-profile payload obfuscator at `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/attach.ts:244-246`, unrelated. So 'what gets typed straight to disk' is a decision with no default. The plan hands it to A4; a human still has to sign the answer.

M2 scope and exit criterion (owner: maintainer, due before M2 is scheduled) — is `ExtensionUIContext` going to reach the shape the M2 plan describes, where `setHeader`/`setFooter` are no-ops and the specifier remap makes `toolRenderers` reachable? If it does not, B1, B2, B3, C2 and D2 all slide and wave 4 cannot start independently. The plan calls this the largest scheduling risk; tail2 can put it at the top of the table with an owner, and cannot resolve it.

Headless/SDK policy for MCP elicitation (owner: whoever owns the MCP surface, due before D1) — no answer exists anywhere in the dossier and both wrong answers are visible at the protocol layer. §11 clause 4 says behaviour follows the decided policy, so D1's DoD cannot be judged until this is written down.

Does a transient notice leave a durable transcript record? (owner: maintainer, not blocking A7) — two different behaviours when scrolling back, and A7 only needs to leave the no-key branch's transcript behaviour exactly as it is. The plan deliberately does not let this gate A7, and tail2 must not let it either.

Should M4/M5 mint a real `ExtensionAPI.registerToolRenderer`? (owner: M4/M5, not an M3 question) — B1 stays a hole with a pinning test. Note the honest limit, which the plan states and the back matter should repeat: a pinning test detects a refactor that deliberately breaks the mechanism; it does not stop an accidental one. A plugin built on the hole can still break.

Do git sidebar and the raw-SSE debug viewer join the shared acceleration model? (owner: whoever implements A3, default: yes) — leaving the SSE viewer out would make the debug app internally inconsistent. Note the asymmetry: the 9th site is `packages/tui/src/apps/git/sidebar.ts:897` using `delta * 3`, not `event.wheel * N`, which is exactly why G4 has to run both greps.

Two unverified claims from the original brief, still unverified: '8 of 8 subsystems' and 'pre-styled ANSI / no cell buffer', plus the counting method behind '7 of 9'. None of them appears in this plan and none should appear in the back matter. A third claim in the same family — that `setFrameProvider` has exactly one non-test call site — was verified and folded into the plan; the other two need either a named feasibility report or deletion.
